skill_traces.query:
Deborah: Hey Jolene, Anna got me a vegan stir-fry the other day - tofu and veg with ginger and soy sauce. It was really tasty! Food is such a wonderful source of pleasure and nourishment. What dishes are comforting to you?
Jolene: One of my favorite dishes is lasagna! Comfort food can be a great pick-me-up. I've got a lot going on with my studies and exams.
Deborah: Have you been able to find time for yourself lately?
Jolene: I've been trying to squeeze in some me-time. Last Friday, I did yoga and meditation to relax. Did you find time for yourself too?
Deborah:  I also did the same, it helped me reset my mind. How does it make you feel?
Jolene: It's amazing how a few quiet moments can work wonders for the soul.
Deborah: Have you been able to get outside lately?
Jolene: I did take Seraphim to the park last Sunday. She loved it and here's a pic.
Deborah: Looks like you guys had fun!
Jolene: We explored new places. People are surprised when they see a tamed snake. What do you like about being outdoors?
Deborah: Hmm... The birds chirping and the breeze gently blowing! It reminds me of what really matters.
Jolene: Yep, it's like a reminder to slow down and appreciate the little things.
Deborah: Is there anything you want to be more mindful of right now?
Jolene: I need to be more mindful of my stress levels and take care of my mental health. Sometimes I get too caught up in my studies and forget to prioritize self-care.
Deborah:  Life can get hectic and it's easy to forget about ourselves. 
Jolene: Exams and deadlines got me feeling overwhelmed. Just look at my to-do list! It seems never-ending... Trying my best but it's been challenging.
Deborah: Your efforts will bear fruit, don't give up!
Jolene: Thanks, Deb. Any tips on studying or time management?
Deborah: My tip is to break it into smaller pieces and set goals for yourself. For time management, planners or schedulers help you stay organized and give you time for yourself. Let me know if you need help with a study plan!
Jolene: I appreciate your help with that.
Deborah: Take care and good luck with your exams. I'll give you a mug just like this one! It encourages.
Jolene: Thanks, Deb! This really cheered me up. All the best with your classes. Bye!
Deborah: Thanks, Jolene! Glad I could bring a smile to your face. Take care and make sure to give yourself some time to relax. Bye!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation includes statements about comfort food (lasagna), activities that provide relaxation (yoga and meditation), and outdoor experiences that bring joy, which are explicit sources of comfort and joy.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Resolve relative time in memory content
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting a memory from a message that contains a relative time expression (e.g., next month, next week, tomorrow), resolve it to the absolute date using the message/session timestamp and include that absolute date in the content.
content: Applies during extraction: when a source message uses a relative time expression (next week, next month, tomorrow, in N days, etc.), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp.
Write the resolved absolute date into the memory content itself (e.g., 'September 2023' instead of 'next month'); do not leave the relative phrase in the stored content.
Set world_start (and world_end if applicable) to the same resolved date so content and metadata are consistent.
Stop after resolving the expression; do not add extra details or searches.

content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
